thread.title: While some fret over a trade war, this stock sector has been on a hot streak - MarketWatch

author: Barbara Kollmeyer
title: While some fret over a trade war, this stock sector has been on a hot streak - MarketWatch
text:
The prospect of a full-blown trade war, and its potential consequences, and what that could mean for this market, has been rattling and enthralling investors in turn.
But it’s been explored up, down and sideways — to the point where pretty much anything else going on for stocks has gotten short shrift.
That Trump tariff noise did ding a lot of stocks yesterday. But quietly in the background, the Nasdaq Composite managed its fourth-straight rise, to cinch its longest win streak since Feb. 20.
That brings us to our call of the day , from trader Larry Tentarelli, who’s all about watching the price and ignoring the noise. The Trend Trading Signals blogger gives us a couple of reasons to pay attention to one particular group of techs: The big money is already there, and new highs are busting out all over.
“There were 140 stocks [Wednesday] with a market cap of $2 billion or greater that made new 52-week highs. Thirty-six of them, or 26%, are in the software industry. This indicates a great amount of institutional interest in the space, with so many names breaking out at once,” Tentarelli tells MarketWatch about Wednesday’s action.
Electronic Arts EA, +0.76% , Microsoft MSFT, +0.21% , Salesforce.com CRM, +0.88% , Adobe ADBE, -0.41% ,Workday WDAY, +0.05% , Shopify SHOP, +2.60% and Square SQ, +3.10% are leaders in that group, he notes.
52-week highs for software names The iShares North-American Tech Software exchange-traded fund IGV, +0.50% also busted to a new high, and it’s made up of many of those names, Tentarelli also points out.
rend Trading Signals iShares North-American Tech Software ETF As for why techs overall are doing better than the rest right now — the Nasdaq is up 7.2%, versus a 2% gain for the S&P 500 year-to-date — Tentarelli says tech is “where the earnings are,” plus companies in the sector have less debt.
Also hoisting a banner for the sector was StockTwits co-founder Howard Lindzon, who noted on his blog how techs are pretty much inured to those negative headlines and themes.
“U.S. tech companies have been dealing with tariffs — pirating, theft and a giant Chinese, Russian and North Korean digital wall — forever,” he notes .
Plus, corporations that get tax breaks will “spend that money on enterprise software and acquisitions that we all have the right to profit from, if we position ourselves correctly,” he says, noting he’s been long business software providers Zendesk ZEN, +2.72% , Okta OKTA, +8.58% and MuleSoft MULE, -0.47% .
Oh, and Intel INTC, -1.27% shot past its Y2K bubble high Wednesday , while Zillow Z, -0.06% has also been cresting to an all-time high, Lindzon adds.
Time to change up the conversation a little?
Key market gauges The Dow DJIA, -0.05% S&P 500 SPX, +0.13% and Nasdaq COMP, +0.21% are moving higher. Asian stocks had a positive session . Meanwhile, data showed China exports unexpectedly surged in February . (The timing’s not great on that data point, given trade tensions .)
Europe SXXP, +1.05% is higher but had pared some gains after the ECB turned more hawkish with its forward guidance. The euro EURUSD, -0.8219% is moving lower , while the dollar DXY, +0.69% is firming up.
